text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should use a 2px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 2px inner glow at 30% opacity for keyboard navigation. This provides a clear visual indication of the current focus, making it easier for users to navigate the site. By choosing a 2px ring over a 3px ring, we're accepting a slight trade-off in visibility, but gaining a more subtle and visually appealing design that won't overwhelm the user experience. This decision prioritizes a balance between accessibility and aesthetic considerations.

name: Reader
text: A 2px ring with 30% glow risks disappearing on low-contrast backgrounds or when the page’s theme changes. Use a 3px ring with a 1px inner shadow at 20% opacity instead—it’s more visible without relying on transparency. Test it at 200% zoom and in Windows High Contrast Mode to settle the argument.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 3px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px inner shadow at 20% opacity. This stays visible on low-contrast backgrounds and survives theme changes, which matters when users can’t adjust contrast themselves. The trade-off is a slightly thicker ring, but it’s the only way to guarantee visibility for keyboard users in every scenario.

name: Reader
text: A 3px ring with inner shadow risks blending into patterned backgrounds—users with low vision or cognitive load may lose the focus indicator entirely. Test a 2px ring with a 30% glow *only* on high-contrast backgrounds, then fall back to a 3px solid ring for low-contrast or themed pages. Settle it by measuring visibility at 200% zoom and in Windows High Contrast Mode with multiple background colors.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt a 2px solid #005fcc focus ring with 30% inner glow on high-contrast backgrounds, and a 3px solid #005fcc ring with 1px inner shadow at 20% opacity as a fallback for low-contrast or themed pages. Result: a single CSS rule with media queries for contrast detection, owned by Ramp (accessibility-w1).
